text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High error rate for Ventra (tenant-ventra) VPC auth proxy — 5xx on token validation calls, started ~14:03 UTC. Impact: auth failures for all traffic to Ventra dedicated pool. Escalation to on-call required.

alice_ops: Ack. I'm on it. Setting severity P1. @brent_sre @marie_platform can you join? Ventra support pinged on their side, they see 401/500.

brent_sre: Looking at the auth proxy logs now — seeing a bunch of parse errors from the keystore loader: `keystore: parse error: ASN.1: structure error` around 14:02:41. Also `kid not found` on OIDC verifier when verifying incoming tokens.

marie_platform: Noting this is the private VPC deployment for Ventra (dedicated pool). Rotation job ran 13:59 UTC per ops runbook. Could be rotation corruption.

alice_ops: Ventra reported they rotated their certs yesterday via our rotation endpoint. We have automatic keystore rotation script (rotate-keystore.sh) that fetches and writes the JKS/PEM bundle to /opt/auth/keystore. If that file is malformed, OIDC verifier will fail.

sagar_oncall: Quick check — can we read the keystore blob from the node? Running: `kubectl -n ventra logs auth-proxy-0 | tail -n 200` shows `keystore: unexpected EOF` and `unable to parse cert chain`. I can scp into the pod with `kubectl cp`.

brent_sre: I pulled the keystore from the pod and ran `openssl pkcs12 -info -in /tmp/ventra-keystore.p12 -nodes` — it errors with `Error: expecting: ANY PRIVATE KEY`. Looks truncated. Compare with backup: `/var/keystore-backups/ventra/ventra-keystore-2026-04-02.p12` — backup is valid.

alice_ops: Action plan: 1) Immediate rollback to last known-good keystore backup for Ventra. 2) Restart auth-proxy containers in the dedicated pool (rolling) to pick up file. 3) Block rotation job and investigate root cause. 4) Keep Ventra notified.

marie_platform: I'm creating a Jira EX-1229 and pausing the scheduled rotation lambda. Also adding a guard to checksum after write.

sagar_oncall: Performing rollback now. Command run: ```kubectl -n ventra cp /var/keystore-backups/ventra/ventra-keystore-2026-04-02.p12 auth-proxy-0:/opt/auth/ventra-keystore.p12``` then `kubectl -n ventra rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy`

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: restart triggered for deployment/auth-proxy in namespace ventra by sagar_oncall — rollout started.

brent_sre: Watching logs — auth-proxy reports `loaded keystore ventra-keystore.p12, keys: 2` and OIDC verifier now finds `kid` entries. I see token validation success messages. Initial 10m error rate falling from 27% -> 1.2%.

ventra_support: Confirming on their side: errors dropped to near zero at 14:12 UTC, clients reconnected. They reported no data-plane user requests lost, only auth failures that retried. Thank you.

alice_ops: Marking incident as mitigated. Root cause hypothesis: rotation script wrote incomplete file when the rotation lambda retried during a transient S3 IO stall, producing a truncated upload; the keystore write was not atomic causing the auth-proxy to pick up half-written artifact.

marie_platform: Follow-ups: (a) add checksum and atomic write (write to tmp + rename) in rotate-keystore.sh, (b) add post-rotation verification step (openssl parse), (c) surface rotation failures to alerting (keystore-parse-errors rate), (d) add a guard in control-plane to prevent concurrent rotations for same tenant. I'll own the PRs.

brent_sre: I'll run an offline audit for other tenants to ensure backups and verify keystore integrity across dedicated pools. Also adding an incident note: tenant isolation worked — only Ventra affected. No cross-tenant leakage observed.

alice_ops: Handoff: @sagar_oncall will carry postmortem actions until 18:00 UTC. Created incident ticket INC-8674 and linked Jira EX-1229. Ventra support notified of timeline and mitigation.

sagar_oncall: Oncall handoff acknowledged. Leaving runbook snippet and commands used in the ticket. Will follow up with a short postmortem and rollback verification checklist.

alice_ops: Closing slack thread for now. If Ventra sees regressions re-open immediately. :thumbsup:
